headline: Moving the styled primitives behind a module boundary changes nothing measurable: every lane renders and ships what it did in the single-file twin, so the styled fold's gap is the `styled(Component)` seam, not the import.

microbench.why: Identical CSS to the Example `tabs`, with the primitives imported instead of declared in place. `vanilla`, `stylex-layers` and the css-prop fold hold 0.806-0.899 ms/1k, unchanged, because none of them resolves anything across modules. The styled fold reads 1.43 ms/1k here against 1.77 in the twin, but its own spread in that cell is 42%, so the boundary does not move it; its library slice is 0.925 ms both ways. `bamboo` (2.13) and `panda` (2.40) match their `tabs` figures too, their classes having been decided at build time in both.

autocannon.why: `vanilla` serves 719 req/s and the css-prop fold 637, within a few percent of the single-file twin. The styled fold serves 435 against 433 there, so the module split costs it nothing measurable. `bamboo` (226) and `panda` (190) again pay for markup rather than styling.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

attribution.why: The two StyleX builds and `vanilla` render in 1.38-1.40 ms and the css-prop fold in 1.47 with a 0.323 ms library slice. `emotion` is again the outlier at 7.55 ms with 5.12 ms of library self-time. `bamboo`'s 3.32 ms carries no styling slice at all: 78.3 of its 87.7 ms JS window is react-dom, the same class-attribute bytes it wrote in `tabs`.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

hydrate.why: Hydration matches the twin lane for lane. Static sheets are pure JS at 48.1-51.8 ms, while `goober` (200 ms) and `styled-components` (202 ms) inject and record 2.26-2.73 ms of recalc plus a 3.5-3.7 ms layout inside the span. Module structure never reaches the browser.

inp.why: Switching the tab re-renders one group at 6.3-7.8 ms across every build-time lane, under 1 ms of JS each. `emotion` spends 0.967 ms in `@emotion/hash` alone and reaches 28.1 ms, `styled-components` 14.1 and `goober` 13.4. The fast cluster ties.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

mount.why: Cold mount reproduces `tabs`: 95.6-100 ms for the static-sheet lanes and 206-232 ms for the runtime injectors, whose mount spans show a 1.66-3.58 ms style recalculation against the others' 0.86-1.04. `panda` mounts at 101 ms here because its `css()` calls are hoisted to module scope and resolve once.

renderTiming.why: One style recalculation for every lane, so the counts tie and the recalc's own cost orders them. `emotion`, `goober` and `styled-components` lay out twice, the extra pass being the reflow their sheet injection forces, and `emotion`'s recalc costs 3.58 ms against the static-sheet lanes' 0.86-1.04.

payload.why: The css-prop fold ships 2.37 kB gzipped, identical to `tabs`, one class per element whichever module declared the rule. `bamboo` (12.0 kB) and `panda` (15.1 kB) ship the same bytes as in the twin as well, most of them class names repeated in the markup. `stylex-layers` 8.14 kB, `cnfast` 22.0 kB.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

nsweep.why: At 4000 groups the static-class lanes hold 31.6-32.7 ms and the css-prop fold 36.0. The styled fold's residual `Yak` scales with n to 70.5 ms. `emotion` (194 ms), `styled-components` (168 ms) and `goober` (147 ms) multiply their per-render hash by 4000 groups.

crossCase: `multifile-composition` is the split-module twin of the Example `tabs` above. The pair isolates the module boundary and finds it costs nothing: the css-prop fold ships 2.37 kB in both and renders at 0.858 against 0.899 ms/1k, `bamboo` at 2.21 against 2.13, and the styled fold's library slice is 0.945 against 0.925 ms. The styled fold's distance from the floor in both is the `styled(Tabs)` seam, where folding cannot resolve a component host to an intrinsic tag.
